abstract: Astrocytes support neuronal function and brain homeostasis and undergo structural and functional remodelling under pathological conditions. Here, we compared astrocytes maintained in serum-containing medium, modelling a blood-brain barrier-compromised reactive state, with serum-free conditions that promote a more physiological arborised phenotype. We examined surface expression and signalling of metabotropic glutamate receptor 5 (mGluR5), {beta}-adrenergic receptors ({beta}-ARs), and pituitary adenylate cyclase-activating polypeptide type 1 receptor (PAC1) as well as expression of excitatory amino acid transporter 2 (EAAT2). Live-cell immunolabelling combined with optophysiological measurements revealed that serum-exposed reactive astrocytes had substantially reduced surface mGluR5 expression and negligible mGluR5-dependent Ca2+ signalling, accompanied by increased expression of EAAT2. Adrenergic stimulation and sustained cAMP elevation restored surface mGluR5 expression and (S)-3,5-dihydroxyphenylglycine (DHPG)-evoked Ca2+ responses while reducing EAAT2 expression despite continued serum exposure. Reactive astrocytes also showed enhanced, prolonged {beta}-AR-mediated cAMP responses that were largely uncoupled from changes in intracellular Ca2+. These findings demonstrate coordinated remodelling of glutamatergic and {beta}-adrenergic signalling in reactive astrocytes. The capacity to restore mGluR5-dependent signalling is retained and strongly regulated by cAMP, suggesting that neuromodulatory pathways can modulate astrocytic glutamate responsiveness independently of a complete reversal of the reactive phenotype.
